Hot Pants
HOT PANTS
noun (Boomer slang)
The fashion trade paper Women’s Wear Daily is credited with naming hot pants in late 1970 for very short, tight shorts worn by women as fashion rather than sportswear, often with boots or tights; they were a craze of 1971 (James Brown’s "Hot Pants," 1971). Pants is short for pantaloons (from Pantalone, the Venetian stock character of the commedia dell’arte), and hot carried its slang sense of sexy. An older vulgar sense of hot pants — sexual desire — existed alongside.

Biblical Definition

Hot pants were the very short, tight shorts that became a women’s fashion craze in 1971 — on city streets, on airline stewardesses, on television dancers. The name said frankly what they were for. The Christian observation: Scripture’s first word about clothing is about covering. After the fall, "they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons" (Gen 3:7), and then "Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them" (Gen 3:21). God improved on the fig leaf; He covered more, not less. The prophet describes the humiliation of proud Babylon in terms of exposure: "make bare the leg, uncover the thigh ... Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen" (Isa 47:2–3). What God treats as the shame of judgment, the 1971 fashion page marketed as liberation. Paul’s counsel is positive, not merely negative: "that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety" (1Ti 2:9), and Peter points to "the hidden man of the heart" as the true ornament (1Pe 3:4). This is not a rule about inches handed down by grumpy men; it is a vision of dignity. A father tells his daughter: you are worth covering, the way God covered Eve. He tells his son: the fashion that uncovers her is not a gift to you but a test, and you must pass it.

Webster 1828 Definition

1971 fashion craze (named by Women’s Wear Daily, 1970) for very short, tight women’s shorts — an uncovering Scripture associates with shame (Isa 47:2–3), set against the God who clothed Adam and Eve (Gen 3:21) and the call to modest apparel (1Ti 2:9).

HOT PANTS, n. pl. (Boomer era, 1970–71) Very short, close-fitting shorts worn by women as fashion. Older vulgar sense: sexual desire ("to have hot pants for someone").

Webster (1828) — PANTALOON, noun 1. A garment for males in which breeches and stockings are in a piece; a species of close long trowsers extending to the heels. 2. A character in the Italian comedy, and a buffoon in pantomimes; so called from his close dress.

Decode for families: the 1971 hot pants are the ancestors of every later fashion that sold exposure as freedom.

Key Scripture

Gen 3:7 — "And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons."

Gen 3:21 — "Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them."

Isa 47:2 — "Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers."

Isa 47:3 — "Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man."

1Ti 2:9 — "In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;"

1Pe 3:4 — "But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price."

Modern Corruption

Hot pants sold exposure as liberation and named the garment for the desire it provoked; Scripture treats uncovering as shame and covering as God’s gift of dignity.

expand to see more

Fashion historians describe hot pants as an act of liberation — women claiming the right to wear what they liked. But the name gives the game away. The garment was designed and named for the eyes of men, and the industry that sold it profited from women’s bodies whether or not the women profited. The sexual revolution often worked that way: it promised freedom and delivered display. Scripture’s word for that display is in Isa 47 and Pro 7:10, and it is not a compliment.

The positive vision is better than the prohibition. God clothed the first couple Himself (Gen 3:21), with garments that cost an animal’s life — the first hint that covering comes by sacrifice. The modest apparel of 1Ti 2:9 is not a burden but a dignity, and the hidden man of the heart (1Pe 3:4) is the beauty that does not need to be uncovered to be seen.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Pantalone (Venetian commedia character) → French pantalon → English pantaloons → American pants + slang hot (sexy) → hot pants (Women’s Wear Daily, 1970).
